title: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
subject: Mathematics
objective: To place p/q, cut each unit into q equal parts and count p parts from 0: right for positive, left for negative.

fill.q: To mark 3/4, divide each unit into ____ equal parts.
The numerator tells how many ____ to count from 0.
Negative rationals lie to the ____ of 0.
A rational number between a and b is (a + b) ÷ ____.

tf.explain: It is negative and less than 1 in size.

tf.q: There is no rational number between 1/2 and 3/4.
To mark 7/4 we count 7 quarter-parts from 0.
Positive rationals are marked to the left of zero.

ar.a: There are infinitely many rationals between 0 and 1.
ar.r: The average of two rationals is a rational between them.

ar.explain: A is false; R is true.

mcq.q: To mark 5/3, each unit is divided into:
How many rationals lie between 0 and 1?
mcq.explain: We can always find another by averaging.

num.q: Find two rational numbers between 1/4 and 1/2 by averaging.

short.q: Explain how to mark −5/4 on the number line.
short.solution: Divide each unit into 4 equal parts; from 0 count 5 parts to the left. That point is −5/4 (between −1 and −2).

short.q: Find three rational numbers between 1/2 and 1.
short.solution: Average: 3/4; then between 1/2 and 3/4: 5/8; between 3/4 and 1: 7/8.
